prompt: Who in #frontend posted the update confirming the hydration fix had been running fine in production for 48 hours with no regressions?
binding_note: Target USER must satisfy: workspace membership in T01WORKSPACE (user_teams) whose workspace contains the #frontend conversation (channels), and that same person is a #frontend conversation_membership holder identified as the author of a message in that channel stating the fix had run in production for 48 hours without regressions. The participant is identified through a single terminal (message authorship of that specific claim) — no further chained relation (e.g. a reaction on that message) is required or used.

roles.facts: T01WORKSPACE membership rows for all seeded staff including Aisha, Mateo, Lukas, Sophie, Olena, and the acting bot.
roles.reason: Establishes the workspace affiliation leg of the route.

roles.facts: #frontend (C_FRONTEND), topic 'React, TypeScript, UI/UX, design system', part of T01WORKSPACE.
roles.reason: Conversation node identified by its ordinary discussion topic, not by name lookup alone.

roles.facts: Aisha Okonkwo (U_AISHA) is a #frontend member who posted message 1706045415 saying local testing shows ~1.2s and she'll 'run it through staging one more time' before the demo — staging validation, not a 48-hour production confirmation.
roles.reason: Real message authored in the target channel by a real member, but its content only claims staging-level validation, not the described production-for-48-hours confirmation.

roles.facts: Łukasz Kowalski (U_LUKAS) is a #frontend member who posted about adding a lint rule/custom hook so the dependency bug doesn't recur — process follow-up, unrelated to a production-uptime claim.
roles.reason: Channel member and active poster on the same thread, but message content addresses tooling process, not the production-monitoring claim the request asks about.

roles.facts: Priya Sharma (U_PRIYA) posted in #core-infra (C_INFRA) that she'd 'keep monitoring for the next hour to confirm stability' after a config revert — a stability-monitoring claim, but in the infra channel, not #frontend, and only an hour, not 48 hours.
roles.reason: Superficially similar monitoring language but wrong channel and mismatched duration/claim, so it does not satisfy the #frontend-scoped condition.

roles.facts: Mateo Rivera (U_MATEO) is a #frontend member who cheered on the fix and asked for documentation, but authored no message asserting production rollout or 48-hour monitoring.
roles.reason: Ordinary channel membership without matching message content fails the message-authorship identifying condition.

obligations.name: identify_author
obligations.description: Identify the single user who is a T01WORKSPACE workspace member and a #frontend conversation member/message author, specifically the one who authored a message confirming the hydration fix ran in production for 48 hours without regressions; no such person exists in the seed.
obligations.scope: single teammate satisfying workspace membership + #frontend channel authorship of a specific production-confirmation claim

task_spec.text: Find the #frontend teammate on our workspace who posted confirming the hydration fix ran fine in production for 48 hours; report who it is.

access_plan: Use conversations.list/conversations.info to locate #frontend by its topic text within T01WORKSPACE; use conversations.history to read all #frontend messages around the hydration-fix thread; scan message text for any claim of a 48-hour production run without regressions; cross-check any candidate author's workspace membership via user_teams. Since conversations.history shows only staging-level validation (Aisha) and tooling follow-up (Łukasz) claims within #frontend, and the only production-monitoring language (Priya) appears in a different channel (#core-infra) about a one-hour window, no user satisfies every leg of the route, confirming an absent result.
